::::::::::::::::::::: {#testing-your-plugin .section}
# Testing your plugin[¶](#testing-your-plugin "Link to this heading"){.headerlink}

::: {#testing-with-flow .section}
## Testing with flow[¶](#testing-with-flow "Link to this heading"){.headerlink}

To test your plugin with flow, you will need to install your plugin. See
the [[Installing your plugin]{.doc}](install_plugin.html){.reference
.internal} page for information on how to do so.
:::

:::::::::::::: {#using-the-testing-module .section}
## Using the testing module[¶](#using-the-testing-module "Link to this heading"){.headerlink}

We can use the [[`PluginTester`{.xref .py .py-class .docutils .literal
.notranslate}]{.pre}](api.html#flogin.testing.plugin_tester.PluginTester "flogin.testing.plugin_tester.PluginTester"){.reference
.internal} class to test our plugin.

[[`PluginTester`{.xref .py .py-class .docutils .literal
.notranslate}]{.pre}](api.html#flogin.testing.plugin_tester.PluginTester "flogin.testing.plugin_tester.PluginTester"){.reference
.internal} takes 3 arguments:

1.  Your plugin

2.  [Your plugin's metadata](#your-plugin-metadata){.reference
    .external}

3.  [Your FlowLauncherAPI
    replacement](#your-flowlauncherapi-replacement){.reference
    .external}

*check out the hyperlinked sections for more information on those
arguments*

Once you have your tester instance all set up, you can use the
[[`test_query()`{.xref .py .py-func .docutils .literal
.notranslate}]{.pre}](api.html#flogin.testing.plugin_tester.PluginTester.test_query "flogin.testing.plugin_tester.PluginTester.test_query"){.reference
.internal} to test your search handlers.

To test your result's context menu, the [[`test_context_menu()`{.xref
.py .py-func .docutils .literal
.notranslate}]{.pre}](api.html#flogin.testing.plugin_tester.PluginTester.test_context_menu "flogin.testing.plugin_tester.PluginTester.test_context_menu"){.reference
.internal} method has been provided to test your context menus.

to test your result's callbacks, simply call their callbacks manually
([[`callback()`{.xref .py .py-func .docutils .literal
.notranslate}]{.pre}](api.html#flogin.jsonrpc.results.Result.callback "flogin.jsonrpc.results.Result.callback"){.reference
.internal}).

::::::: {#example .section}
### Example[¶](#example "Link to this heading"){.headerlink}

Here is a simple plugin:

:::: {.highlight-default .notranslate}
::: highlight
    from flogin import Plugin, Query, Result, ExecuteResponse

    my_plugin = Plugin()

    class MyResult(Result):
        async def callback(self):
            await my_plugin.api.show_notification("Flogin", "result's callback has been triggered")
            return ExecuteResponse()

    @my_plugin.search()
    async def blanket(q: Query):
        return MyResult("Blanket Handler Called")
:::
::::

And here is a simply testing script for it:

:::: {.highlight-default .notranslate}
::: highlight
    import asyncio

    from flogin.testing import PluginTester
    from flogin import Query

    # Since we use the `show_notification` api method in our result callback, we need to implement it in our replacement class.
    class FakeFlowAPI:
        async def show_notification(self, *args):
            print(f"showing notification with {args!r}")


    async def main():
        # Because we don't use the metadata at all, we can just use some bogus data.
        metadata = PluginTester.create_bogus_plugin_metadata()

        # Creating our plugin tester object
        tester = PluginTester(my_plugin, metadata=metadata, flow_api_client=FakeFlowAPI())

        # Creating our query object. In this example, this query would represent a query which was `bambo`, with our plugin's keyword being `bambo`.
        query = Query(
            raw_text="bambo",
            keyword="bambo",
            text="",
        )

        # Testing our search handlers and getting the response
        response = await tester.test_query(query)

        # getting our result
        result = response.results[0]

        # printing out result's title
        print(f"Result title: {result.title}")

        # Executing our result's callback
        await result.callback()


    asyncio.run(main())
:::
::::
:::::::

::: {#your-plugin-metadata .section}
### Your Plugin metadata[¶](#your-plugin-metadata "Link to this heading"){.headerlink}

If you pass [`None`{.docutils .literal .notranslate}]{.pre} to the
[`metadata`{.docutils .literal .notranslate}]{.pre} argument, flogin
will attempt to retrieve the metadata from your [`plugin.json`{.docutils
.literal .notranslate}]{.pre} file.

In cases where that is not available or you need to customize your
metadata, the [[`create_bogus_plugin_metadata()`{.xref .py .py-func
.docutils .literal
.notranslate}]{.pre}](api.html#flogin.testing.plugin_tester.PluginTester.create_bogus_plugin_metadata "flogin.testing.plugin_tester.PluginTester.create_bogus_plugin_metadata"){.reference
.internal} and [[`create_plugin_metadata()`{.xref .py .py-func .docutils
.literal
.notranslate}]{.pre}](api.html#flogin.testing.plugin_tester.PluginTester.create_plugin_metadata "flogin.testing.plugin_tester.PluginTester.create_plugin_metadata"){.reference
.internal} methods have been provided.

The [[`create_plugin_metadata()`{.xref .py .py-func .docutils .literal
.notranslate}]{.pre}](api.html#flogin.testing.plugin_tester.PluginTester.create_plugin_metadata "flogin.testing.plugin_tester.PluginTester.create_plugin_metadata"){.reference
.internal} classmethod provides a cleaner ui for creating a
[[`PluginMetadata`{.xref .py .py-class .docutils .literal
.notranslate}]{.pre}](api.html#flogin.flow.plugin_metadata.PluginMetadata "flogin.flow.plugin_metadata.PluginMetadata"){.reference
.internal} object, with some arguments being optional, and being
auto-generated.

The [[`create_bogus_plugin_metadata()`{.xref .py .py-func .docutils
.literal
.notranslate}]{.pre}](api.html#flogin.testing.plugin_tester.PluginTester.create_bogus_plugin_metadata "flogin.testing.plugin_tester.PluginTester.create_bogus_plugin_metadata"){.reference
.internal} provides a very fast way to generate a "valid" metadata
object, by filling it with random data.
:::

::::::: {#id1 .section}
### Your FlowLauncherAPI replacement[¶](#id1 "Link to this heading"){.headerlink}

If you do not use [[`FlowLauncherAPI`{.xref .py .py-class .docutils
.literal
.notranslate}]{.pre}](api.html#flogin.flow.api.FlowLauncherAPI "flogin.flow.api.FlowLauncherAPI"){.reference
.internal} in the code that you are testing, then the default filler
object will do just fine.

However if you use the api at all in the code you want to test, you will
want to create a FlowLauncherAPI replacement class for testing and pass
it to the [`flow_api_client`{.docutils .literal .notranslate}]{.pre}
argument in your plugin tester's constructor.

When creating your replacement class, make sure to implement any and all
API methods that you use, and respond accordingly inside of them.

For example, lets say I use the [[`open_settings_menu()`{.xref .py
.py-func .docutils .literal
.notranslate}]{.pre}](api.html#flogin.flow.api.FlowLauncherAPI.open_settings_menu "flogin.flow.api.FlowLauncherAPI.open_settings_menu"){.reference
.internal} method. I would implement that method into my replacement
class, which might look something like this:

:::: {.highlight-default .notranslate}
::: highlight
    class MyFlowAPI:
        async def open_settings_menu(self):
            print("-- Settings menu has been opened --")
:::
::::

That one is pretty easy due to it not returning anything, or doing
anything that may affect the plugin. Let's take another example,
[[`open_settings_menu()`{.xref .py .py-func .docutils .literal
.notranslate}]{.pre}](api.html#flogin.flow.api.FlowLauncherAPI.open_settings_menu "flogin.flow.api.FlowLauncherAPI.open_settings_menu"){.reference
.internal}. You can always do something similiar to what we did with
[[`open_settings_menu()`{.xref .py .py-func .docutils .literal
.notranslate}]{.pre}](api.html#flogin.flow.api.FlowLauncherAPI.open_settings_menu "flogin.flow.api.FlowLauncherAPI.open_settings_menu"){.reference
.internal}, however for this example we will handle what will happen if
we try to add a keyword to our own plugin. To do this, we will pass our
plugin to our api class, and later use that to check the plugin ids, and
add the keyword.

:::: {.highlight-default .notranslate}
::: highlight
    class MyFlowAPI:
        def __init__(self, plugin):
            self.plugin = plugin

        async def add_keyword(self, plugin_id: str, keyword: str):
            if plugin_id == self.plugin.metadata.id:
                self.plugin.metadata.keywords.append(keyword)

            print(f"-- Added {keyword!r} keyword to {plugin_id!r} --")
:::
::::
:::::::
::::::::::::::

::::::: {#writing-tests .section}
## Writing Tests[¶](#writing-tests "Link to this heading"){.headerlink}

If you ever decide to write tests for your plugin, the testing module
can be used for that too. For this example, we will be using the
[pytest](https://pypi.org/project/pytest/){.reference .external}
library, with the
[pytest-asyncio](https://pypi.org/project/pytest-asyncio/){.reference
.external} plugin.

Here is a simple plugin:

:::: {.highlight-default .notranslate}
::: highlight
    from flogin import ExecuteResponse, Plugin, Query, Result

    my_plugin = Plugin()


    class MyResult(Result):
        async def callback(self):
            await my_plugin.api.show_notification(
                "Flogin", "result's callback has been triggered"
            )
            return ExecuteResponse()


    @my_plugin.search(text="egg")
    async def easter_egg(q: Query):
        return "You found the easter egg!"


    @my_plugin.search()
    async def blanket(q: Query):
        return MyResult("Blanket Handler Called")
:::
::::

Here is an example of writing tests for the plugin:

:::: {.highlight-default .notranslate}
::: highlight
    import pytest

    from flogin import Query
    from flogin.testing import PluginTester
    from plugin import my_plugin


    @pytest.fixture
    def tester():
        metadata = PluginTester.create_bogus_plugin_metadata()
        return PluginTester(my_plugin, metadata=metadata)


    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_blanket_handler(tester: PluginTester):
        class FakeFlowAPI:
            async def show_notification(self, title: str, text: str):
                assert title == "Flogin"
                assert text == "result's callback has been triggered"

        tester.set_flow_api_client(FakeFlowAPI())

        query = Query(
            raw_text="bambo",
            keyword="bambo",
            text="",
        )
        response = await tester.test_query(query)

        result = response.results[0]

        assert result.title == "Blanket Handler Called"

        execute_response = await result.callback()
        assert execute_response.hide is True


    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_easter_egg_handler(tester: PluginTester):
        query = Query(raw_text="bambo egg", keyword="bambo", text="egg")
        response = await tester.test_query(query)

        result = response.results[0]

        assert result.title == "You found the easter egg!"
:::
::::

Good next steps:

- [pytest-asyncio
  docs](https://pytest-asyncio.readthedocs.io/en/latest/index.html){.reference
  .external}

- [pytest docs](https://docs.pytest.org/en/stable/index.html){.reference
  .external}

- [[Testing Module API Reference]{.std
  .std-ref}](api.html#testing-module-api-reference){.reference
  .internal}
